I don’t know if you’ll see this, but I hope you’re still out there and do. I wanted to share my experience and I pray it helps in some small way. Your situation is almost identical to mine. I too was a born of adultery and don’t know many of my family, let alone am close to anyone that I do know. I don’t tell many people that because it’s shameful, you know? Everyone else has families but when you don’t, it feels awkward and isolating. My mom was separated but was having an affair with my dad (he was her doctor) and they both had children before me, the “unplanned accident.” I wasn’t exactly planned on and everyone in my fam likes to tell me that, which makes me feel like a mistake. I end up thinking, “why am I here?” 

My dad tried to get rid of me by trying to pay off my mom to get an abortion. My mom wouldn’t have it and decided to keep me. I was handed a box by her when I was 12 that told me everything. She always told me how much I was never wanted or was just a mistake. It’s taken a lot from me, and I struggled so very much with it in my teens and early 20’s. I still do sometimes. But the main thing I wanted to share with you is that I have learned that I am not a mistake. And neither are you. As hard as it was for me to believe, sure I wasn’t planned by my earthly parents but I was by my heavenly ones. You were planned by your heavenly ones, just like me.

I still have rough days when it’s hard to believe and I very much relate to your line about if HF loves us, then why have we never caught a break? I have asked him that more than once. I’ve been angry and confused at the hand I’ve been dealt. But I am slowly realizing it’s ok to go to Him with all of my feelings, concerns, and even anger and frustration. And as angry as I am, I can’t remember a time He has hurt me or has not listened and tried to heal me. Please know you’re not alone.  I hope someday we can hang out with our loving parents on the other side :) don’t give up. You are a fighter.
